question: Who founded the Tattvabodhini Sabha that was set up to explore spiritual truth?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Debendranath Tagore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Tattvabodhini Sabha was founded by Debendranath Tagore in 1839 in Calcutta to spread rational, Vedanta-based spiritual truth and reform Hindu religious thought. (तत्त्वबोधिनी सभा — देवेन्द्रनाथ टैगोर)

 

• Debendranath Tagore was the son of Dwarkanath Tagore and the father of Rabindranath Tagore. He later merged the Tattvabodhini Sabha's followers into the Brahmo Samaj, becoming one of its principal leaders after Raja Ram Mohan Roy.

 

• The Sabha published the Tattvabodhini Patrika, an influential journal that promoted Brahmoism, Bengali literature, and rational religious enquiry.

 

• Debendranath Tagore is often called 'Maharshi' for his deep engagement with the Upanishads and Vedantic philosophy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Brahmo Samaj was originally founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828 as the Brahmo Sabha; Debendranath Tagore revived and reorganised it institutionally in the 1840s.

 

• Keshab Chandra Sen later led a breakaway faction called the Brahmo Samaj of India in 1866 after differences with Debendranath Tagore.

 

NOTE

 

• Keshab Chandra Sen (Option 1): He was a later Brahmo Samaj leader who split from Debendranath Tagore's faction; he did not found the Tattvabodhini Sabha.

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy (Option 2): He founded the Brahmo Sabha (1828), the precursor of the Brahmo Samaj, not the Tattvabodhini Sabha.

 

• Dayanand Saraswati (Option 4): He founded the Arya Samaj in 1875, a separate reform movement, and had no connection to the Tattvabodhini Sabha.

question: In which method of cooking is food heated slowly over a source of heat and cooked by high heat and air convection depending on the position of the food in relation to the fire?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Spit-roasting.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Spit-roasting is a dry-heat cooking method in which food (typically meat) is skewered on a rotating spit and cooked slowly over or beside an open source of heat. (स्पिट-रोस्टिंग — भूनने की विधि)

 

• The food is cooked by a combination of direct radiant heat and air (convection) currents, and the intensity of cooking varies with the position of the food relative to the fire as the spit rotates, giving even, slow cooking with a characteristic crisp exterior.

 

• It is one of the oldest known cooking methods and is a dry-heat method, distinct from moist-heat methods like poaching, stewing, and braising.

 

• Spit-roasting is commonly used for whole birds, joints of meat, and barbecued preparations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dry-heat cooking methods include roasting, baking, grilling, spit-roasting and frying; moist-heat methods include boiling, poaching, steaming, braising and stewing.

 

• Braising and stewing are combination/moist-heat methods that use both dry searing and slow moist cooking in a covered pot with liquid.

 

NOTE

 

• Braising (Option 2): Food is first seared, then cooked slowly in a small amount of liquid in a covered pan — a moist-heat method, not dependent on distance from an open fire.

 

• Poaching (Option 3): Food is gently cooked by immersion in liquid kept just below boiling point — a moist-heat method.

 

• Stewing (Option 4): Food is cut into pieces and cooked slowly, fully immersed in liquid — a moist-heat method.

question: In which of the following animal phyla, is the body divided into head, thorax and abdomen?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arthropoda.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Phylum Arthropoda is characterised by a body typically divided into head, thorax and abdomen (or a fused cephalothorax and abdomen), a chitinous exoskeleton, and jointed appendages. (आर्थ्रोपोडा — संधिपाद प्राणी)

 

• Arthropoda is the largest animal phylum, comprising insects, crustaceans, arachnids and myriapods, and accounts for over three-fourths of all known animal species.

 

• The name 'Arthropoda' comes from Greek *arthron* (joint) and *podos* (foot), referring to their jointed legs.

 

• Growth in arthropods occurs through moulting (ecdysis) of the exoskeleton.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Annelida (segmented worms like earthworms) have a body divided into similar repeating segments, not head-thorax-abdomen.

 

• Insecta, a class within Arthropoda, is the classic example showing the clear head-thorax-abdomen division.

 

NOTE

 

• Annelida (Option 1): Body is metamerically segmented into similar ring-like segments, e.g. earthworm, leech — no head/thorax/abdomen division.

 

• Mollusca (Option 2): Body is divided into head, muscular foot and visceral mass (e.g. snail, octopus), not head-thorax-abdomen.

 

• Chordata (Option 4): Possess a notochord and dorsal nerve cord; body plan (e.g. in vertebrates) is head, trunk and tail, not head-thorax-abdomen.

question: Which state had the first female Governor in independent India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sarojini Naidu became the Governor of Uttar Pradesh in 1947, making her the first woman Governor of an Indian state in independent India. (सरोजिनी नायडू — उत्तर प्रदेश की प्रथम महिला राज्यपाल)

 

• She served as Governor of United Provinces (later Uttar Pradesh) from 1947 until her death in 1949.

 

• Sarojini Naidu was also known as the 'Nightingale of India' and had earlier been the first Indian woman President of the Indian National Congress (Kanpur session, 1925).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sarojini Naidu was a prominent poet and freedom fighter, closely associated with Mahatma Gandhi and the Quit India Movement.

 

• Other notable women governors include Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit (Maharashtra) and Sheila Dikshit (Kerala), who came later.

 

NOTE

 

• West Bengal, Rajasthan, Gujarat (Options 1, 2, 4): None of these states had the first female Governor of independent India — that distinction belongs to Uttar Pradesh with Sarojini Naidu.

question: Who among the following was the head of the Diwan-i-Insha department under the Delhi sultanate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dabir-i-Khas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the Delhi Sultanate, the Diwan-i-Insha was the department of state correspondence, responsible for drafting and issuing royal orders (farmans) and official letters. Its head was called the Dabir-i-Khas. (दीवान-ए-इंशा — दबीर-ए-ख़ास)

 

• The Dabir-i-Khas drafted royal decrees, maintained official records of correspondence, and communicated the Sultan's orders to provincial officials.

 

• The Delhi Sultanate administration had several such departments (Diwans), each headed by a specific officer, forming a systematic central bureaucracy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Diwan-i-Arz (military department) was headed by the Ariz-i-Mumalik, responsible for recruitment and organisation of the army.

 

• The Diwan-i-Risalat dealt with religious matters and appeals, headed by the Sadr-us-Sudur.

 

NOTE

 

• Barid-i-Mumalik (Option 2): He was the head of the intelligence/news-reporting department (Diwan-i-Barid), not the correspondence department.

 

• Amir-i-Dad (Option 3): He was the officer responsible for implementing the orders of the Qazi-i-Mumalik, essentially a chief justice-related judicial officer.

 

• Wakil-i-Dar (Option 4): He was in charge of the royal household and personal affairs of the Sultan, not the correspondence department.

question: Which is the correct sequence of oceans according to size (from largest to smallest) ?
option_1: Pacific Ocean > Antarctic Ocean > Indian Ocean > Atlantic Ocean
option_2: Pacific Ocean > Indian Ocean > Antarctic Ocean > Atlantic Ocean
option_3: Pacific Ocean > Atlantic Ocean > Indian Ocean > Antarctic Ocean
option_4: Pacific Ocean > Indian Ocean > Atlantic Ocean > Antarctic Ocean
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pacific Ocean > Atlantic Ocean > Indian Ocean > Antarctic Ocean.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• By area, the world's oceans rank: Pacific Ocean (largest) > Atlantic Ocean > Indian Ocean > Southern/Antarctic Ocean > Arctic Ocean (smallest). (महासागर — प्रशांत महासागर सबसे बड़ा)

 

• The Pacific Ocean covers roughly 165 million sq km, more than all the Earth's landmass combined, and is bounded by Asia/Australia and the Americas.

 

• The Atlantic Ocean (~106 million sq km) separates the Americas from Europe and Africa.

 

• The Indian Ocean (~70 million sq km) is the third largest, bounded by Asia, Africa and Australia; the Southern (Antarctic) Ocean surrounding Antarctica is the second smallest, and the Arctic Ocean is the smallest of all.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Southern Ocean was formally recognised as the fifth ocean by the National Geographic Society in 2021.

 

• The Pacific Ocean contains the Mariana Trench, the deepest point on Earth (Challenger Deep, ~11,034 m).

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4: Each misplaces the Antarctic (Southern) Ocean or Indian Ocean in the ranking; the factually correct descending order by area is Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Antarctic (Southern), Arctic.

question: In which year did Antoine Lavoisier publish ‘Methods of Chemical Nomenclature’, which included the rules for naming chemical compounds that are still in use today?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1787.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Antoine Lavoisier, along with collaborators including Guyton de Morveau, Berthollet and Fourcroy, published 'Méthode de nomenclature chimique' (Methods of Chemical Nomenclature) in 1787. (एंटोनी लावोज़िए — रासायनिक नामकरण पद्धति, 1787)

 

• This work established a systematic, logical system for naming chemical compounds based on their constituent elements, replacing the earlier arbitrary and alchemical names.

 

• Many of its core naming conventions (e.g. based on combining elements/radicals) laid the foundation for modern chemical nomenclature systems still refined by IUPAC today.

 

• Lavoisier is widely regarded as the 'Father of Modern Chemistry' for his work on combustion, the law of conservation of mass, and this nomenclature system.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lavoisier's other landmark work, 'Traité élémentaire de chimie' (Elementary Treatise on Chemistry), was published in 1789 and is considered the first modern chemistry textbook.

 

• Lavoisier disproved the phlogiston theory and correctly identified the role of oxygen in combustion and respiration.

 

NOTE

 

• 1783, 1780, 1790 (Options 1, 2, 3): These years do not correspond to the publication of the Méthode de nomenclature chimique, which was published in 1787.

question: At the 108th Indian Science Congress concluded at Rashtrasant Tukdoji Maharaj Nagpur University on 7 January 2023. Who among the following won the Dr CV Raman Birth Centenary Award?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prof SR Niranjana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 108th Indian Science Congress was held at Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj Nagpur University and concluded on 7 January 2023, with the theme 'Women Empowerment and Sustainable Development with Science & Technology'. (भारतीय विज्ञान कांग्रेस — नागपुर विश्वविद्यालय, 2023)

 

• Prof SR Niranjana, a plant pathologist, was conferred the Dr CV Raman Birth Centenary Award at this Congress for her contributions to plant sciences.

 

• The Dr CV Raman Birth Centenary Award is given by the Indian Science Congress Association (ISCA) to honour outstanding contributions in science.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indian Science Congress Association (ISCA) was founded in 1914 and holds its annual Congress inaugurated traditionally by the Prime Minister of India.

 

• The 109th Indian Science Congress was scheduled to be hosted at Lovely Professional University, Punjab.

 

NOTE

 

• Prof Subhash Chandra Parija, Dr Ranjan Kumar Nandy, Dr Kaushal Prasad Mishra (Options 1, 2, 4): These were not the recipients of the Dr CV Raman Birth Centenary Award at the 108th Indian Science Congress; the award went to Prof SR Niranjana.

question: On the occasion of National Youth Day on 12th January 2023, also known as Vivekananda Jayanti, the Government of India gave awards to 82 of the best ________ of the country.
solution_text:
The correct answer is agripreneurs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On National Youth Day, 12 January 2023 (Swami Vivekananda's birth anniversary), the Government of India honoured 82 of the best agripreneurs of the country with National Awards, recognising young entrepreneurs contributing to agriculture and allied sectors. (राष्ट्रीय युवा दिवस — कृषि-उद्यमी सम्मान)

 

• The awards were given under a scheme promoting agripreneurship among youth, encouraging innovative agri-startups and value-addition in the farm sector.

 

• National Youth Day commemorates the birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda (12 January 1863) and is celebrated nationwide with youth festivals and events.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The National Youth Festival 2023 was inaugurated in Karnataka by the Prime Minister, coinciding with the celebrations.

 

• The theme of Vivekananda Jayanti celebrations typically centres on Swami Vivekananda's ideals of youth empowerment and nation-building.

 

NOTE

 

• Engineers, doctors, teachers (Options 1, 3, 4): The 82 National Youth Day awards for 2023 were specifically given to agripreneurs, not to these professional groups.

question:
Identify the option that arranges the following states’ literacy rates in descending order, according to Census 2011.

A. Kerala

B. Himachal Pradesh

C. Haryana
solution_text:
The correct answer is (A), (B), (C).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Census 2011, literacy rates were: Kerala ≈ 93.91%, Himachal Pradesh ≈ 82.80%, and Haryana ≈ 75.55%. (जनगणना 2011 — केरल सर्वाधिक साक्षर राज्य)

 

• In descending order, this gives Kerala > Himachal Pradesh > Haryana, i.e. (A), (B), (C).

 

• Kerala has consistently topped Indian states in literacy rate since Census 1991, owing to strong historical investment in public education and social reform movements.

 

• Haryana, despite strong economic indicators, had a comparatively lower literacy rate among the three states listed, partly due to a lower female literacy rate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• As per Census 2011, Bihar had the lowest literacy rate (≈61.80%) among Indian states.

 

• India's overall literacy rate as per Census 2011 was 74.04% (male 82.14%, female 65.46%).

 

NOTE

 

• (A), (C), (B) (Option 1): Incorrectly places Haryana above Himachal Pradesh.

 

• (B), (A), (C) (Option 2): Incorrectly places Himachal Pradesh above Kerala.

 

• (C), (B), (A) (Option 3): Reverses the entire correct order (ascending instead of descending).

question: Under Statutory liquidity ratio, commercial banks are required to keep a fraction of _________ in form of liquid assets.
solution_text:
The correct answer is total demand and term deposits.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) requires every commercial bank in India to maintain a certain percentage of its Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL) — i.e. total demand and term deposits — in the form of liquid assets such as cash, gold, or approved government securities. (सांविधिक तरलता अनुपात — मांग व सावधि जमा)

 

• SLR is fixed and regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

 

• Unlike CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio), which must be kept with the RBI in cash form, SLR assets are held by the bank itself and can include cash, gold and approved securities.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• SLR is one of RBI's key monetary policy tools, used to control liquidity, inflation, and credit expansion in the economy.

 

• Both CRR and SLR are calculated as a percentage of a bank's Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL).

 

NOTE

 

• Current deposits (Option 1): These form only a part of demand deposits, not the full base on which SLR is calculated.

 

• Term deposits (Option 3): These alone (excluding demand deposits) do not constitute the full base for SLR calculation.

 

• Saving deposits (Option 4): These are only a component of demand and time deposits combined, not the entire base used for SLR.

question: Deepika Pallikal is associated with ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is squash.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Deepika Pallikal Karthik is a top Indian squash player, the first Indian woman to break into the world's top 10 squash rankings. (दीपिका पल्लीकल — स्क्वैश खिलाड़ी)

 

• She has won multiple medals at the Commonwealth Games (including gold in women's doubles squash) and the Asian Games.

 

• She is married to Indian cricketer Dinesh Karthik.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable Indian squash players include Saurav Ghosal and Joshna Chinappa, Deepika's frequent doubles partner.

 

• India won a historic gold medal in the mixed doubles squash event at the 2022 Commonwealth Games (Saurav Ghosal–Dipika Pallikal).

 

NOTE

 

• Billiards, chess, cricket (Options 2, 3, 4): Deepika Pallikal is not associated with these sports; she is specifically a squash player.

question: Nor Westers are dreaded evening thunderstorms seen in _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bengal and Assam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nor'westers (locally called Kalbaisakhi in Bengal and Bordoichila in Assam) are dreaded pre-monsoon evening thunderstorms accompanied by strong winds, hail and heavy rain, occurring mainly in West Bengal, Assam, Odisha and parts of Bihar/Jharkhand. (नॉर्वेस्टर — काल बैसाखी, पश्चिम बंगाल व असम)

 

• They occur typically during March to May (the pre-monsoon 'hot weather' season) in the late afternoon/evening, caused by intense local heating and moist air convection.

 

• These storms are locally beneficial for tea, jute and rice cultivation despite their destructive nature, as they bring pre-monsoon rainfall crucial for these crops.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Similar local pre-monsoon storms include 'Aandhi' in northern India and 'Mango showers' in Kerala/Karnataka (which benefit mango and coffee crops).

 

• Nor'westers are also known for causing thunder, lightning and sometimes hailstorms that can damage standing crops.

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab and Haryana (Option 2): These regions experience 'Loo' (hot dry winds) in summer, not Nor'westers.

 

• Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): These are not the typical regions associated with Nor'westers.

 

• Telangana and Maharashtra (Option 4): Nor'westers are not characteristic of these southern/western regions.

question: Which of the following institutions was set up in 1982 in order to streamline credit facilities to farmers at a national level?
solution_text:
The correct answer is NABARD.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) was established on 12 July 1982, based on the recommendations of the B. Sivaraman Committee, to streamline and provide credit facilities for agriculture and rural development at the national level. (नाबार्ड — कृषि व ग्रामीण विकास बैंक, 1982)

 

• NABARD took over the agricultural credit functions earlier performed by the RBI and the Agricultural Refinance and Development Corporation (ARDC).

 

• NABARD's headquarters is located in Mumbai, Maharashtra.

 

• It plays a central role in refinancing rural credit institutions like RRBs, cooperative banks, and financing rural infrastructure through the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• NABARD also promotes financial inclusion initiatives such as the Self-Help Group (SHG)-Bank Linkage Programme.

 

• The Chairman of NABARD is appointed by the Government of India in consultation with the RBI.

 

NOTE

 

• NEDFI (Option 1): The North Eastern Development Finance Corporation, set up in 1995, promotes industrial development in the North-East, not national agricultural credit.

 

• IFCI (Option 3): The Industrial Finance Corporation of India, established in 1948, was India's first development finance institution, focused on industrial finance.

 

• SIDBI (Option 4): The Small Industries Development Bank of India, set up in 1990, focuses on financing micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), not agriculture.

question: Who was the winner of ICC Men’s T20 World Cup– 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Australia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Australia won the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2021, defeating New Zealand by 8 wickets in the final held at Dubai International Cricket Stadium, UAE, on 14 November 2021. (आईसीसी टी20 विश्व कप 2021 — ऑस्ट्रेलिया विजेता)

 

• This was Australia's first-ever ICC Men's T20 World Cup title, with Mitchell Marsh named Player of the Match in the final for his unbeaten 77.

 

• The tournament was hosted by the BCCI but played in the UAE and Oman due to COVID-19 related restrictions in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• David Warner was named Player of the Tournament in the 2021 T20 World Cup.

 

• The subsequent ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2022, held in Australia, was won by England, defeating Pakistan in the final.

 

NOTE

 

• India (Option 1): India was eliminated in the Super 12 stage of the 2021 tournament and did not reach the final.

 

• West Indies (Option 2): West Indies, the defending champions from 2016, failed to progress beyond the Super 12 stage in 2021.

 

• England (Option 4): England lost to New Zealand in the semi-final of the 2021 T20 World Cup, not the winner that year.

question: Bhortal dance is famous in _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bhortal (Bhaortal) dance is a traditional dance form of Assam, performed with large cymbals called 'tal' or 'bhortal', and is closely associated with the Sattriya cultural and monastic tradition founded by Srimanta Sankardev. (भोरताल नृत्य — असम)

 

• It is typically performed by male dancers as part of devotional/ritual performances in Sattras (Vaishnavite monasteries) of Assam, often during festivals and religious congregations.

 

• The dance involves intricate rhythmic movements combined with the playing of large cymbals, requiring great skill and coordination.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sattriya, the classical dance form of Assam, was given classical dance status by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000.

 

• Other important dance/cultural forms of Assam include Bihu dance and Ojapali.

 

NOTE

 

• Odisha (Option 1): Known for Odissi classical dance, not Bhortal.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 2): Known for folk forms like Karma and Matki, not Bhortal.

 

• Punjab (Option 3): Known for Bhangra and Giddha, not Bhortal.

question: In November 2022, which of the following Union Ministries has launched a month-long campaign titled, ‘Nai Chetna–Pahal Badlav Ki’ – A Community-led National Campaign against Gender-Based Discrimination?
option_3: Ministry of Women and Child Development
option_4: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Rural Development.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, launched the month-long 'Nai Chetna – Pahal Badlav Ki' campaign in November 2022, a community-led national campaign against gender-based violence and discrimination. (नई चेतना – पहल बदलाव की — ग्रामीण विकास मंत्रालय)

 

• The campaign is implemented through the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), leveraging the network of Self-Help Groups (SHGs) to raise awareness against gender-based violence in rural India.

 

• It runs annually as part of the 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence (25 November – 10 December), aligning with International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Subsequent editions, 'Nayi Chetna 2.0' and 'Nayi Chetna 3.0 – Pahal Badlaav Ki', were launched in later years (2023, 2024) continuing the same theme.

 

• The DAY-NRLM mobilises rural women into SHGs to promote livelihoods, financial inclusion and social empowerment.

 

NOTE

 

• Ministry of Culture (Option 2): Not the ministry behind this campaign; it deals with cultural heritage and promotion.

 

• Ministry of Women and Child Development (Option 3): Works on women/child welfare schemes but did not launch this specific SHG-based rural campaign.

 

• Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (Option 4): Focuses on welfare of SCs, OBCs, and marginalised groups, not this particular campaign.

question: Hindustani vocalist Pandit M Venkatesh Kumar was awarded which of the following awards in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalidas Samman.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit M Venkatesh Kumar, a renowned Hindustani classical vocalist of the Kirana-Gwalior gharana, was honoured with the Kalidas Samman 2022 by the Government of Madhya Pradesh for his contribution to classical music. (कालिदास सम्मान — पंडित एम वेंकटेश कुमार)

 

• The Kalidas Samman, instituted by the Madhya Pradesh government in 1980-81, is one of India's most prestigious awards, given across the fields of classical music, classical dance, theatre, and plastic arts.

 

• Venkatesh Kumar was earlier honoured with the Padma Shri (2016) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (2012) for Hindustani vocal music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kalidas Samman is named after the classical Sanskrit poet-dramatist Kalidasa and is presented annually by the Madhya Pradesh government at Ujjain.

 

• Ustad Rashid Khan and Pandit Jasraj are among other eminent Hindustani vocalists who have received major national honours for classical music.

 

NOTE

 

• Tagore Puraskar (Option 1): Officially the Tagore Ratna or Sangeet Natak Akademi's Tagore Award, a different national award, not the one received in 2022 by Venkatesh Kumar in this context.

 

• Sangeet Natak Akademi (Option 3): Venkatesh Kumar had already received this award in 2012, not in 2022.

 

• Sangeeta Kalanidhi (Option 4): This is a prestigious award given by the Madras Music Academy for Carnatic music, not applicable to a Hindustani vocalist like Venkatesh Kumar.

question: Which of the following elements is highly effective for making a permanent magnet?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Steel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Steel (an alloy of iron and carbon) is highly effective for making permanent magnets because it has high retentivity (remanence) and high coercivity, allowing it to retain magnetism strongly once magnetised. (स्टील — स्थायी चुंबक निर्माण)

 

• A good permanent magnet material must have high retentivity (retains magnetism after the magnetising field is removed) and high coercivity (resists demagnetisation).

 

• In contrast, soft iron has high retentivity but low coercivity, making it ideal for temporary/electromagnets, not permanent magnets.

 

• Alloys like Alnico (aluminium-nickel-cobalt) and steel are commonly used for permanent magnets due to these magnetic properties.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Soft iron is used in electromagnets, transformer cores and telephone receivers because it can be magnetised and demagnetised quickly.

 

• Ferromagnetic materials include iron, nickel, cobalt and their alloys; among the given options, only steel exhibits strong ferromagnetic behaviour suited to permanent magnets.

 

NOTE

 

• Zinc, Aluminium, Copper (Options 1, 2, 3): These are paramagnetic/diamagnetic materials with negligible magnetic properties and are not used to make permanent magnets.

question: Which of the four Vedas contains a collection of magic spells and charms to fend off evil spirits and diseases?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Atharva Veda.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Atharva Veda is the fourth of the four Vedas and is distinct in containing hymns, magic spells, charms and incantations meant to ward off evil spirits, diseases, and misfortune, alongside hymns on daily life, medicine and philosophy. (अथर्ववेद — तंत्र-मंत्र व रोग निवारण)

 

• It is attributed to sages Atharvan and Angiras, and is sometimes called the 'Veda of magical formulas'.

 

• Unlike the other three Vedas, which are primarily liturgical (used in yajnas/rituals), the Atharva Veda also deals with folk practices, healing, and everyday concerns of ordinary people.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Rig Veda is the oldest Veda, a collection of hymns/mantras praising various deities.

 

• The Sama Veda consists mainly of musical chants derived from the Rig Veda, used in rituals.

 

• The Yajur Veda contains prose mantras and rituals to be performed during yajnas (sacrificial rites).

 

NOTE

 

• Rig Veda (Option 1): The oldest and most sacred Veda, composed of hymns to deities like Agni and Indra — not focused on magic spells.

 

• Sama Veda (Option 2): Primarily concerned with musical notation and chants for rituals.

 

• Yajur Veda (Option 3): Concerned with the procedural details and mantras for performing sacrifices, not magic and charms.

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the Right against Exploitation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 23.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 23 of the Indian Constitution, under the Right against Exploitation (Articles 23-24), prohibits traffic in human beings, begar (forced labour), and other similar forms of forced labour. (अनुच्छेद 23 — शोषण के विरुद्ध अधिकार)

 

• Article 24 complements it by prohibiting the employment of children below 14 years in factories, mines, or other hazardous occupations.

 

• Together, Articles 23-24 form the Right against Exploitation, one of the six Fundamental Rights guaranteed under Part III of the Constitution.

 

• Violation of Article 23 is a punishable offence under law, and it applies against both the State and private individuals.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The six Fundamental Rights are: Right to Equality (14-18), Right to Freedom (19-22), Right against Exploitation (23-24), Right to Freedom of Religion (25-28), Cultural and Educational Rights (29-30), Right to Constitutional Remedies (32).

 

• The Right to Property (Article 31) was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Constitutional Amendment, 1978.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 22 (Option 1): Deals with protection against arrest and detention in certain cases, part of the Right to Freedom.

 

• Article 21 (Option 3): Guarantees the Right to Life and Personal Liberty, part of the Right to Freedom.

 

• Article 20 (Option 4): Provides protection in respect of conviction for offences (e.g. no ex-post-facto law, double jeopardy, self-incrimination), part of the Right to Freedom.

question: By which of the following acts was a bicameral legislature introduced in India at the centre level?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Government of India Act of 1919.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Government of India Act, 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) introduced a bicameral legislature at the centre for the first time, comprising the Council of State (Upper House) and the Legislative Assembly (Lower House). (गवर्नमेंट ऑफ इंडिया एक्ट 1919 — द्विसदनीय व्यवस्थापिका)

 

• This Act also introduced dyarchy (dual government) in the provinces, dividing subjects into 'reserved' and 'transferred' categories.

 

• It expanded the size of legislatures and introduced direct elections for the first time in India, along with separate electorates for Sikhs, in addition to Muslims (introduced earlier in 1909).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Government of India Act, 1935 further expanded bicameralism and introduced provincial autonomy and an All-India Federation (never fully implemented).

 

• The Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) introduced separate electorates for Muslims but did not create a bicameral central legislature.

 

NOTE

 

• Indian Councils Act of 1861 (Option 1): Restored legislative powers to Bombay and Madras presidencies and introduced Indians into the Viceroy's council, but no bicameral central legislature.

 

• Regulating Act of 1773 (Option 2): Created the office of Governor-General of Bengal and an Executive Council; it predates any Indian legislature altogether.

 

• Government of India Act of 1935 (Option 4): Retained/expanded bicameralism established in 1919 but was not the Act that first introduced it.

question: The National Highway Authority of India (NHAI) was operationalised in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1995.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) was constituted through the National Highways Authority of India Act, 1988, but it was actually made operational (functional) in 1995. (राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग प्राधिकरण — 1995 में कार्यशील)

 

• NHAI is responsible for the development, maintenance and management of National Highways in India and works under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.

 

• NHAI implements major highway programmes such as the National Highways Development Project (NHDP) and the Bharatmala Pariyojana.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• NHAI's headquarters is located in New Delhi.

 

• The Golden Quadrilateral project, connecting Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata, was a major highway project executed under NHAI.

 

NOTE

 

• 2005 (Option 1): Not the year of NHAI's operationalisation.

 

• 2000 (Option 2): Not the year of NHAI's operationalisation.

 

• 1993 (Option 3): Not the correct year; NHAI's Act was passed in 1988 but it became functional in 1995.

question: How many times in a year is the Bihu festival celebrated in Assam?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bihu festival of Assam is celebrated three times a year: Rongali/Bohag Bihu (April, marking the Assamese New Year and spring), Kati/Kongali Bihu (October, associated with the harvest/lean season), and Bhogali/Magh Bihu (January, marking the end of the harvesting season). (बिहू पर्व — असम, वर्ष में तीन बार)

 

• Rongali Bihu is the most significant of the three, celebrated with feasting, folk dance (Bihu dance) and music, marking the onset of the agricultural season.

 

• Bhogali Bihu is a harvest festival marked by community feasts and bonfires (Meji), while Kati Bihu is a more austere, prayer-focused occasion when granaries are usually empty.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bihu dance, performed during Rongali Bihu, is a vibrant folk dance of Assam characterised by brisk movements to the beat of dhol, pepa, and other traditional instruments.

 

• Assam's Bihu festivals reflect the state's agrarian culture and the agricultural calendar of rice cultivation.

 

NOTE

 

• 5, 4, 2 (Options 1, 2, 4): These do not correctly represent the number of Bihu celebrations in a year; Bihu is celebrated exactly three times annually.

question: Which of the following groups of classical dancers is related to Kathak?
option_1: Yamini Krishnamurthy, Shobha Naidu and Swapnasundari
option_2: Sitara Devi, Shaswati Sen and Urmila Nagar
option_3: Alarmel Valli, Malavika Sarukkai and Sucheta Chaphekar
option_4: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Kiran';src: url('https://appxcontent.kaxa.in/fonts/Kiran.ttf') format('truetype');} </style>Kumkum Mohanty, Sonal Mansingh and Kiran Sehgal
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sitara Devi, Shaswati Sen and Urmila Nagar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sitara Devi, Shaswati Sen, and Urmila Nagar are all renowned exponents of Kathak, the classical dance form of North India associated with the Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras gharanas. (कथक नृत्य — सितारा देवी, शास्वती सेन)

 

• Sitara Devi was a legendary Kathak exponent of the Kalka-Bindadin (Lucknow) gharana, often called the 'Empress of Kathak'.

 

• Shaswati Sen is a leading disciple of Pandit Birju Maharaj, one of the foremost Kathak gurus, while Urmila Nagar is also a well-known Kathak dancer trained in the Lucknow gharana.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The major Kathak gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras; Pandit Birju Maharaj was the most prominent Kathak exponent of recent times.

 

• Kathak is characterised by intricate footwork, fast spins (chakkars), and storytelling through expressive gestures (abhinaya).

 

NOTE

 

• Yamini Krishnamurthy, Shobha Naidu, Swapnasundari (Option 1): These are exponents of Bharatanatyam/Kuchipudi/Vilasini Natyam, not Kathak.

 

• Alarmel Valli, Malavika Sarukkai, Sucheta Chaphekar (Option 3): These are noted Bharatanatyam dancers, not Kathak.

 

• Kumkum Mohanty, Sonal Mansingh, Kiran Sehgal (Option 4): These dancers are primarily associated with Odissi, not Kathak.
